abstraction: mem_alloc(&u->zeeb, MESH_BACKING_LINEAR); where{NULL,(size_t)u->zeeb}; lease_buffer(zeeb,&base.buffer,&base.offset)
handles: An issue's communicator-owned buffers and combine landing area get one linear lease, then a base pointer for slot_laid to cut.
replacement: lifetime allocation of the issue's virtual pages onto physical pages; no linear backing request and no base pointer in the compiler
note: MESH_BACKING_LINEAR is itself a hand-picked map: contiguity requested so byte offsets from one base stay valid.

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: write_binding_slot (ncclMeshInvocationIndex % instances) * layout.instance_stride
handles: A WRITE's per-invocation storage slot is picked by cyclic index times a byte stride.
replacement: lifetime allocation yields the invocation -> (virtual page -> physical page) map; final lowering specializes the literal page index

abstraction: displacement = frame*write->bytes + first*element_bytes | frame*stride + write_displacement(...) | x->offset; shifted(origin, displacement)
handles: Each entry's bytes are located as a byte displacement from its buffer's where.
replacement: composition of the step's logical piece with the declared view layout and the page map; bytes appear only at final lowering

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: origin = st->read[step] (send buffer read in place) else st->buffer[step->buffer]
handles: A SEND reads the caller's send buffer in place instead of its step's numbered buffer.
replacement: the source page map is the declared operand's map composed with the step's piece; sharing pages with the send operand is a lifetime-allocation outcome, never a hand choice

abstraction: x->data = shifted(area, used); used += page_up(bytes)
handles: Each combine's landing gets its own pages of the issue's landing area by a bump offset.
replacement: lifetime allocation of each landing's virtual pages (live from landing to its combine) onto physical pages

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: step->buffer < 2 -> view_at(c, buffer==0, x->offset): buffer numbers 0/1 stand for the caller's send/recv where
handles: An all-to-all's steps name the caller's buffers by fixed buffer numbers.
replacement: steps name the declared operand's page map by operand identity; composition with the piece gives its pages

abstraction: mesh_landing_next over m->spans (struct mesh_dma_span with region offsets)
handles: Numerical readiness runs are derived by walking the placed DMA span table.
replacement: readiness is the preimage of the packet cuts in logical coordinates; the DMA spans are emitted only at final lowering

abstraction: mem_alloc(&u->progress, LINEAR); memset(u->progress); lease_buffer(u->progress,&base.buffer,&base.offset)
handles: A group's progress words get a linear lease and a Metal base so each word is base + 8*k.
replacement: progress words are pages of the function's page map, allocated by lifetime allocation; their initial value is a declared page effect; addresses at final lowering

abstraction: shifted(base, at*sizeof(uint64_t)) for spans_ready, ready, copied, summed
handles: Each SEND, landing, channel and combine is given its progress word by a byte offset in the lease.
replacement: composition of the word index layout with the words' page map; specialization at final lowering

abstraction: ((uint64_t *)u->progress)[at] = m->pages.n
handles: The host writes each entry's unit count into its readiness word at preparation.
replacement: a declared initialization effect on the word's page, evaluated by the final lowering

abstraction: lease_offset((uint64_t *)u->progress + at): region offset of a word
handles: The bridge's ready and summed words are named by region offset recovered from a host pointer.
replacement: the word's physical page is the page map's image; no inverse from a pointer

abstraction: owned_end/owned_add(&u->owned, held->address | u->tables | u->progress)/owned_begin keyed by lease address
handles: The leases an issue's entries read are held open for retirement, identified by their addresses.
replacement: lifetime allocation keyed by page identity: the image of the issue's page maps names the pages it holds

abstraction: mem_alloc(&u->tables, length, MESH_BACKING_LINEAR)
handles: The span tables, bridge tables and requirement lists of an issue get one linear lease.
replacement: lifetime allocation of the table pages; the bridge's linear-read requirement is a declared layout constraint, not a byte cursor

abstraction: address_of(x->data); in_region; lease_at(address); position = address - held->address; lease_runs
handles: An entry's host address is inverted to its lease and physical runs, and checked to lie in a live lease.
replacement: the entry's physical pages are the image of its page map; a page table names only live region pages, so no inverse and no check

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: write_span_index(write, step, invocation) = step*occurrences + invocation % occurrences
handles: A WRITE entry reuses one of a fixed number of prepared span trains cyclically.
replacement: lifetime allocation gives each invocation's page map; span trains are specialized per distinct image at final lowering

abstraction: write->spans + span_first[index] + frame*units; mesh_page_run_add(..., spans[k].offset) region offsets
handles: A WRITE entry's physical runs are rebuilt from its prepared DMA spans' region offsets.
replacement: image of the WRITE's page map; spans emitted only at final lowering

abstraction: made = (struct mesh_dma_span *)((char *)u->tables + length); made[unit].offset = mesh_page_run_offset(&physical, at); mesh_dma_span_valid(M, span)
handles: Each entry's DMA spans are built in region offsets and written into the table lease during placement.
replacement: specialization at final lowering: SGEs are the page map's image cut at packet boundaries, written by the effector

abstraction: x->table = lease_offset(made); lease_buffer(u->tables,&u->linkable,&linked); linking.region = lease_offset(tables); linking.offset = linked + (tables - u->tables)
handles: The bridge and the GPU name each table by region offset and Metal-buffer offset recovered from host pointers.
replacement: tables are pages of the function's page map; region page and buffer offset are its image, specialized at final lowering

abstraction: (struct mesh_zwoggle *)((char *)u->tables + length); x->requirement = (uint64_t *)((char *)u->tables + length)
handles: Bridge tables and requirement lists are placed by a byte cursor in the tables lease.
replacement: lifetime allocation of table pages, composed with each table's record layout; byte addresses only at final lowering

abstraction: m->spans[k].bytes read from the DMA span table
handles: A SEND's alignment with the landing it forwards is measured over the placed span tables.
replacement: packet cuts in logical coordinates (span residues) answer the alignment; the DMA table is not a chooser input

abstraction: m->offset - from->offset: byte offsets of SEND and landing in their buffer
handles: A relay SEND's first unit is located inside the landing it forwards by subtracting buffer byte offsets.
replacement: preimage of the SEND's pages in the landing's page map gives the unit position in logical coordinates

abstraction: m->dep_summed = from->summed_word (a region offset from lease_offset)
handles: A relay SEND waits on its landing's summed word, named by region offset.
replacement: the word is a page of the page map named by identity; its address is specialized at final lowering

abstraction: const char *M; (const char *)channels[q].view.landed - M; summed_word
handles: A SEND's prerequisite words are named as region offsets computed by pointer subtraction from the region base.
replacement: words are page identities in the page map; offsets from M are emitted only at final lowering

abstraction: list = (struct mesh_zwoggle_after *)(m->requirement + 1); m->requirement[0] = n; list[r] = {words[r], 0}
handles: The host writes each SEND's requirement list into the bridge-read table lease during preparation.
replacement: the requirement relation is chooser data over page identities; the effector writes the bridge list at final lowering

abstraction: o->c < m->c: order of struct call pointers
handles: Whether a reading SEND is earlier than an overwriting landing is decided partly by comparing call record addresses.
replacement: order by declared call ordinal in the composed schedule

abstraction: interval meets over m->spans[j].offset (region-offset DMA spans) of landings and SENDs
handles: A landing that overwrites bytes an outgoing SEND of the same issue reads is found by intersecting region-offset spans.
replacement: preimage of the intersection of the landing's and the SEND's page-map images across the issue; the order follows from the composition

abstraction: list[r] = {(const char *)comm->channels[q].view.sent - M, 0} written through m->requirement
handles: A landing's wait on another channel's sent count is written as a region offset into the bridge list.
replacement: the sent word is a page identity; the bridge list entry is written by the effector at final lowering

abstraction: interval meets of this issue's landing spans with every laid issue's SEND spans in region offsets
handles: A landing into caller's pages that other issues' SENDs read is ordered after the last such SEND.
replacement: preimage of the image intersection between the issue's landing page map and other issues' SEND page maps (lifetime relation), never region-offset intervals

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: binding instance number taken to mean the same caller pages at the same list places
handles: An issue reuses the overwrite readers of its definition's issue of the same binding instance.
replacement: equality of page-map images decides reuse of the relation; the instance index is not a page identity

violation: chooser picks a map by hand
abstraction: v->instance != a->instance: cyclic binding instance as page identity
handles: A landing's after-requirements are taken from laid issues of the same binding instance.
replacement: the reader set is the preimage of the landing's pages in the other issues' SEND maps

abstraction: (ch->view.sent - M), (ch->view.landed - M), (ch->view.ready - M), M + z->after, "%p" of the issue
handles: A diagnostic record of the bridge tables reads region offsets and dereferences M + offset.
replacement: the record prints the page-map relation (page identities, list positions); region offsets only from the final lowering's own record
note: Diagnostics only (MESH_PLAN_RECORD); it still holds the region base pointer.
